q1_issues.issue: The concessive connective's second argument is the family ENTITY sk_family_1 rather than a reified eventuality for the subordinate clause 'being in the same language family', so Despite relates a state to a thing instead of the two eventualities the connective rule requires.

The Degree level 'only_distantly' welds the focus particle 'only' onto the adverb into an invented compound symbol, where the level slot takes the surface adverb lemmatized and 'only' is a focus particle with its own opaque atom.
The Degree atom is predicated of hungarian alone, although the relatedness it modifies holds of the Hungarian-Finnish pair, so singling out one relatum is unlicensed and asymmetric.

q2_gaps: A static relational / membership clause used as a connective-atom endpoint ('Despite BEING IN the same language family, ...'): the endpoint-reification recipe is defined only for a copular PROPERTY state (sk_<prop> witness + Experiencer + flat Member), while PartOf / LocatedIn relations mint no eventuality at all, so a concessive connective has no second argument to take.

'only' scoping over a degree adverb ('only distantly related') — a scalar upper-bound reading; the focus-particle section defines (Only <filler> <event>) over a clause constituent, and the Degree section's level slot takes a bare intensifier/downtoner, so neither covers a particle stacked on a degree adverb.
notes: The symmetric-predicate encoding (Related + Symmetric Related), the language_family compound genus and the shared sk_family_1 witness forced by 'the same' are all correct. The reified state carrying two Experiencer atoms has no explicit licence — the collective multi-filler pattern is stated for Agent — but it is the natural analog for a stative symmetric endpoint.
